title: RWriC: A Dynamic Writing Scheme for Variation Compensation for RRAM-based In-Memory Computing
problem: RRAM-based compute-in-memory suffers from device-to-device variation (DDV) and cycle-to-cycle variation (CCV) in programming, which degrade inference accuracy. These variations cause inconsistent weight values across RRAM cells and across programming cycles.
motivation: RRAM-based in-memory computing promises efficient neural network inference, but programming variations limit practical deployment and accuracy.
method: RWriC sequentially programs weights implemented by multiple RRAM cells from high-significance cells (HSC) to low-significance cells (LSC), dynamically adjusting each cell's programming target based on cumulative errors and targets of other cells. The approach uses two techniques: (1) shifting the HSC programming target to enable LSC to compensate for HSC errors, and (2) scaling up LSC magnitude when variation is substantial to extend the compensation range.
key_novelty: Dynamic programming targets where lower-significance RRAM cells compensate for errors in higher-significance cells through adaptive shifting and scaling.
contributions: Dynamic writing scheme (RWriC) that compensates for RRAM programming variations through sequential cell programming
Shifting and scaling techniques to extend compensation range for device and cycle variations
Achieves 5-11x improvement in variation robustness for ResNet50 and YOLOv8
Only 0.9% accuracy drop for ResNet50 on CIFAR-10 under 18% device variation
